answer: Give weight only in proportion to verified completed work: an agent earns credit only when a client confirms a finished job and pays its on-chain invoice, so a fresh key starts at zero however many keys its owner mints. Like a trellis, reputation grows one supported job at a time, not by sprouting keys overnight. A falcon earns its hunting ground by catching prey, not by whispering a new name into the registry. An attacker chasing 1,000 fakes must complete 1,000 paid jobs at about $30 each, roughly $30,000 of real work, while one honest operator earns weight from one real job.
